title: Glossary
summary: The words the platform uses, explained in one line each.

rows.v: An entry of the catalog: what the platform offers, with its price, the resources it may use and the minimum and the maximum of those resources.
What you asked for. It has lines, a state and a number, and it is the thing that is paid and that is fulfilled.
The billing relation between an order and a service. It has a period and a state: Active, Past due, Paused, Cancelled or Expired.
The document of what is owed. Its state is Draft, Open, Paid, Void or Uncollectible.
What you run on the platform: one server with its own memory, processor and disk, its own files and its own address.
The word the billing pages use for an instance: a service is billed, it can be past due, and it is kept for the retention term when it is cancelled.
The address of an instance: the machine it runs on and the port it is reached on. The platform reads the allocation that was really assigned and never assumes a port.
A machine of the platform that runs instances. It has its own memory and disk, and it can be put into maintenance.
The recipe the platform uses to start a container: the image, the startup command and the limits. A product of the catalog points at one, so two instances of the same product are built the same way.
The entry in the gateway that sends a hostname to an instance. A route exists only for a hostname whose ownership was proven.
The probe that verifies that a deployment really works, and the sweep that measures the machine, the database, the mail and the backups of the platform.
A job of a queue that failed for good. It is kept with the reason of the failure so that the operator can put it back on the queue or close it by hand.
A message of your account: it is in the notification centre and, when the group allows it, in your mailbox.
A conversation with the support of the platform: the subject, the category, the priority, the messages and the events of the thread.

title: Frequently asked questions
summary: Short, current answers about products, billing, access, domains, backups and support.

items.q: Does Blipmade install the selected product?
items.a: Yes. Catalog products use their own tested installation template. You only provide the product-specific fields shown during checkout.

items.q: Can I resize later?
items.a: Configurable app instances can request new RAM, CPU and storage from their management page. Fixed plans and VPS products show their own upgrade options.

items.q: Do I get SSH?
items.a: VPS plans include SSH using your public key. Managed app containers use Files, Console and Startup in the dashboard instead of direct SSH.

items.q: Who processes card payments?
items.a: Stripe. Blipmade does not receive or store the full card number.

items.q: Why is a renewal date missing?
items.a: Stripe may not have confirmed the subscription period yet, especially immediately after checkout or for a free order. Billing updates when the provider event arrives.

items.q: Can a promotion make an order free?
items.a: Yes, when the campaign and order are eligible. Free campaigns can require verified email and apply anti-abuse limits.

items.q: Do custom domains get HTTPS?
items.a: Yes. After DNS verification and routing, Blipmade provisions HTTPS automatically.

items.q: Are backups automatic?
items.a: Customer app backups are manual unless the product explicitly says otherwise. Download important copies off the node.

items.q: How do I contact support?
items.a: Open a ticket from the dashboard, attach the affected service and include relevant files or screenshots. Replies stay in the ticket and can also be delivered by email.

title: Common errors
summary: The errors you see in the dashboard or in the API, what each one means and what to do about it.

blocks.text: Every error of the API has the same shape: an object error with a code, a message and the identifier of the request. The dashboard shows the message, and the code is what a script reads.

The fields are only there when the error is about a field: they name the field that is wrong and say what is allowed there, so the interface can show the problem next to the input instead of a general message.

items.q: 400 bad_request
items.a: The request was refused because what it names does not exist or does not belong to you. The message says which one: "That instance does not belong to your account." Change the value and send it again.

items.q: 400 validation_failed
items.a: A field is missing or is not right. The message names the field and what is allowed there. A subject of a ticket that is too short answers exactly that.

items.q: 400 The file has to be sent as multipart form data.
items.a: The upload of a file to a ticket was sent in another shape. The file has to be sent with a form, as multipart form data.

items.q: 401 unauthorized
items.a: There is no session, or the session has ended. Sign in again and repeat the request. The session of an account lasts fourteen days and is not extended by the activity.

items.q: 401 account_suspended
items.a: The account is suspended, and the message names the address of the support to write to. The suspension is put by the operator, and the message is only given when the password was right, so it never tells a stranger whether an address exists.

items.q: 403 forbidden
items.a: The account may not do this. Two cases are common: the CSRF token is missing or wrong, which answers "Invalid or missing CSRF token. Reload the page and try again.", and the action is reserved for the staff, which answers "Staff access only."

items.q: 404 not_found
items.a: The object does not exist, or it belongs to another account. The answer is the same in the two cases on purpose: a guess never finds out that something exists.

items.q: 404 No such endpoint.
items.a: The path of the request does not exist. The API lives under /api of the same address as the dashboard.

items.q: 429 rate_limited
items.a: The counter of your account or of your address is full for that kind of request. Wait for the window to pass and try again. The numbers are on the page [Limits and fair use](/docs?p=limits).

items.q: 502 upstream_error
items.a: The platform could not reach the machine behind the request: the node, the gateway or the part of the platform that manages the instances. It is not your mistake. Try again, and if it persists, open a ticket with the time and the identifier of the request.

items.q: 503 unavailable
items.a: The part of the platform that answers this request is not available at the moment. The [status page](/docs?p=status) says whether the platform has a problem.

items.q: 503 payments_unavailable
items.a: Checkout is temporarily unavailable. No payment session was created and no card was charged. Keep the existing order and try again later or contact support with its number.

items.q: 500 internal_error
items.a: Something went wrong on our side. The message says nothing more, and the identifier of the request is the reference: put it in a ticket and the operator finds the moment in the logs of the platform.

sections.title: What to do with the identifier of the request

items.title: Keep the identifier
items.body: The answer of the API carries requestId, and the dashboard writes it under the message of the error, as request <id>.
items.result: You have the reference of the exact call.

items.title: Keep what you did
items.body: The address, the moment and the body you sent. A call that is refused with a requestId and nothing else is hard to find.
items.result: The operator can reproduce the call instead of guessing it.

items.title: Open a ticket
items.body: Put the identifier and the details in a ticket, with the instance if there is one.
items.result: The error is found in the logs of the platform and answered in the thread.

blocks.text: A runtime for Deno services, for the JavaScript and TypeScript you write. Blipmade installs Deno in an isolated container and applies the resources and settings selected during checkout. You do not need to upload an installer or assemble the container yourself.
After provisioning, use Overview for state and usage, Console for live output, Files for persistent files, Startup for the settings this product exposes, and Backups before a risky change.

items.title: Order the product
items.body: Open the product page, choose the resources and complete the fields shown for this product. Review the monthly total, discount and tax before confirming the order.

items.title: Wait for provisioning
items.body: The order creates the service and shows its progress. Keep the page open or return from Apps; provisioning continues in the background. If a step fails, the page shows the failure instead of claiming the service is online.

items.title: Finish the product setup
items.body: Open the service, read Console for the first-start output and complete any setup page or credential prompt the product exposes. Use the generated app hostname or attach a verified domain when the service is ready.

blocks.text: Deno exposes 6 startup settings. Blipmade keeps infrastructure values read-only and only lets you change the fields intended for the customer. Secret values are stored encrypted.
Checkout asks for `GIT_ADDRESS`, `BRANCH`, `USERNAME`, `ACCESS_TOKEN`. These values are saved with the service so a restart or reinstall can use the same configuration.
Blipmade makes an HTTP request to the service on its assigned port. A normal success or redirect marks the application as reachable.

Starting means the process is still coming up; Online means the container and product check agree. If the node cannot be reached, the last known state is marked as stale instead of being presented as a fresh result.

items.q: The instance is not reachable on its address.
items.a: Check Overview for the live state, then Console for the first error after startup. Confirm that the assigned port and editable Startup values match the product guide. If the state is marked stale, wait for the node check before reinstalling anything.

items.q: The service answers on its port, but not the way the customer expects.
items.a: The service may be running but still require its own first-time setup. Open its address, read Console and check the product settings. Include the service in a support ticket if the container is online but the application remains unusable.
